 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J.

1. Heard Sri Vijay Shantam, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 164 of 2020, under Sections 323, 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Gandhi Park, District Aligarh during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, this is second bail application filed on behalf of applicant and however first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J vide order dated 24.01.2023 but as His Lordship has been transferred from this Court and this Bench is dealing with such matters, therefore, instant second bail application is listed today before this Bench.
4. He further submits, however, applicant is husband of the deceased and as per allegation his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of torture in connection to demand of dowry but in the present matter applicant is in jail since 17.05.2020 i.e. for last more than five and half years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.

5. He further submits, in the charge-sheet there are total seven witnesses and out of seven witnesses only four witnesses could be examined and considering the speed of trial there is no hope of its early disposal.
6. He next submits, for offence under Section 304B IPC minimum punishment is seven years which can be extended up to life and applicant has already served more than 50% of the minimum punishment.
He further submits, considering the fact that prima facie it appears to be a case of suicidal death there is no likelihood that applicant may be awarded with maximum punishment.
7. He further submits, applicant is not having any criminal history.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that deceased i.e. wife of applicant died due to hanging and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 17.05.2020 i.e. for last more than five and half years.
9.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. This is second bail application filed on behalf of applicant and first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J but as His Lordship has been transferred from this Court and this Bench is dealing with such matters, therefore, instant second bail application is listed before this Bench.

It appears, however, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of torture in connection with demand of dowry but post Ajay vs State Of U.P. on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118000452/
2 mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, it appears to be a case of suicidal death and applicant is in jail since 17.05.2020 i.e. for last more than five and half years.

11. Further, for offence under Section 304B IPC minimum punishment provided is seven years which though can be extended up to life imprisonment and applicant has already served more than 50% of the minimum punishment and considering the fact that prima facie it appears to be a case of suicidal death, the argument advanced by learned counsel for applicant that it is highly improbable that applicant may be awarded maximum punishment cannot be completely ruled out.
12. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant - Ajay be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

(Sameer Jain,J.) January 6, 2026 AK Pandey  Ajay vs State Of U.P. on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118000452/
